parts:
Hi Jay.

Try:

chp<-getChipEffectSet(plm)

readUnits(plm,units=1) will give you the chip effects (i.e.
expression levels).

To get it in matrix format, either you can 'unwrap' the list
structure that readUnits returns or you can use the 'extractMatrix'
function.

Awhile ago, I made a function to get the expression values from the
chip effect set, that may be useful for you. See below. You would
run it as:

d<-getExprs(chp)

... and then you could write.table that to a file if you wanted.

getExprs <- function(ces, ...) {
cdf <- getCdf(ces);
theta <- extractMatrix(ces, ..., returnUgcMap=TRUE);
ugcMap <- attr(theta, "unitGroupCellMap");
un<-getUnitNames(cdf, ugcMap[,"unit"]);
rownames(theta) <- un
log2(theta)
}

Cheers,
Mark

Hi J.

Are you using the Ensembl CDF from the google website? If so, the
rownames of theta should be 'ENSGXXX' already ... note that this is
NOT the first column of theta ... though if you write it to a text
file with row.names=T, then it'll be the first column there.

If you are getting transcript_cluster_ids, then I'm a bit confused as
to how you've processed the data. Maybe give me you're entire list
of commands, or at least a 'print(csN)' and a 'print(getCdf(csN))' ...

As far as transforming to ENST labels, there is a subtle point here.
The CDF file has been generated as 'gene-centric', which basically
means that all the probes for a give GENE (i.e. all known transcripts
if more than one) are treated as one unit. If you want individual
transcript estimates, that's a different question and not one that I
have addressed. Maybe someone else on the list has. But, if
differential splicing is what you are after, then I'd suggest trying
FIRMA (see google page).

Hope that helps.
Mark

There is also a function that returns the group names
(readCdfGroupNames) from a cdf, basically like Mark's suggested code.
I've done code something like this before:

plmNoMergeTissue<- ExonRmaPlm(csNTissue, mergeGroups=FALSE)
cesNoMergeTissue<-getChipEffectSet(plmNoMergeTissue)
pbsetSumm<-extractMatrix(cesNoMergeTissue,returnUgcMap=TRUE,units=1:3)
#or whatever units you want
pbsetNames<-readCdfGroupNames(getPathname(getCdf(cesNoMergeTissue)),unit=1:3)
rownames(pbsetSumm)<-unlist(pbsetNames)

Note that I use the cdf of cesNoMergeTissue, which is the monocell cdf
with one entry per group allowed, and not the original cdf.

Best,
Elizabeth

I've been working on two methods to help out here. They will probably
show up in the next release. In the meantime, you can grab them as
patches, i.e. just do once:

downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

The methods work like this:

> data <- extractDataFrame(ces, units=312:314)
> str(data)

$ unit : int 312 312 312 312 312 312 312 312 ...
$ group : int 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 ...
$ cell : int 4775 4776 4777 4778 4779 4780 ...

$ huex_wta_cerebellum_C: num 6.73 40.53 13.58 16.59 ...
$ huex_wta_heart_A : num 6.72 57.15 97.25 77.89 ...

So when extract data as a data.frame the (unit,group,cell) map is
contained in the first three columns. The rest of the columns are the
names of the arrays. extractDataFrame() calls extractMatrix()
internally and takes the same arguments.

> ugpMap <- data[,c("unit", "group", "cell")]
> ugNames <- getUnitGroupNamesFromUgcMap(getCdf(ces), ugcMap=ugcMap)
> data <- cbind(ugNames, data)
> str(data)

$ huex_wta_cerebellum_C: num 6.73 40.53 13.58 16.59 ...
$ huex_wta_heart_A : num 6.72 57.15 97.25 77.89 ...

The above methods should work in all cases regardless of value on
'mergeGroups' and similar arguments that select a subset of the
groups. (I might consider adding an argument 'addNames' to
extractDataFrame() to encapsulate the latter method call).

Let me know if works as expected

/Henrik
